Step by step guide to your PhD journey
Step by step guide to your PhD journey
On this page, you can find an overview of important official steps to take, milestones to achieve, and processes to be aware of during your doctoral journey.
Steps towards your PhD
1st Step: Getting a PhD position
First you need the commitment of a supervisor from the CoBeNe faculty
Second, secure funding either through one of our advertised open CoBeNe calls, or through one of the individual PhD calls specified by the respective group leader
Another option is bringing your own funding, e.g. from third-party funding agencies
2nd Step: Admission to UniVie
Your admission as a doctoral student to a doctoral programme at the University of Vienna is processed by the Center of Doctoral Studies.
Requirements:
You must hold a master's degree (or equivalent) in the intended field of research (or closely related)
You must already be accepted by a CoBeNe supervisor (see Step 1)
Process:
The application for admission takes place via u:space. All information about the admission process can be found on the pages of the Center of Doctoral Studies
In the study programme, SPL54: Psychology, Cognition, Behavior, and Neuroscience, you have to choose your dissertation field in the respective doctoral programme
3rd Step: Join VDS CoBeNe
Note: Becoming a member of VDS CoBeNe is a separate process from admission to UniVie (see Step 2)!
Once you are admitted to UniVie, please read and sign our Code of Good Practice to officially become a member of the VDS CoBeNe
Sign up for one of our Welcome and Information meetings to get to know your CoBeNe office team, your peers, and to learn about the PhD programme
VDS CoBeNe will guide and support you through your doctoral journey
First year - Entry phase
Overview
Early milestones in the entry phase (typically about 12 months) include submitting your research proposal (Exposé), publicly presenting your project to faculty (FÖP – fakultätsöffentliche Präsentation), and signing the doctoral thesis agreement with your supervisor.
If you were admitted with supplementary coursework, you must complete it within two semesters and before the FÖP.
The public presentation is a prerequisite for topic approval; if successful, the Directorate of Doctoral Studies usually confirms your topic and supervisor(s) immediately. If not approved, you may withdraw, revise your proposal, and resubmit for approval.
Steps to take
Sign the Code of Good Practice to join VDS CoBeNe
Attend a VDS CoBeMe Welcome and Info Meeting
Take part in the Welcome Days for PhDs (each winter semester)
Plan your public presentation at the faculty (FÖP)
Present your research proposal and pass FÖP
Submit your doctoral thesis agreement within 4 weeks after FÖP
Within your second semester, organize your first Thesis Advisory Committee (TAC) meeting
If applicable, do supplementary coursework
CoBeNe events and courses
For beginning PhD candidates, VDS CoBeNe offers the following opportunities and resources:
Welcome and Information meeting and onboarding support
Introduction to CoBeNe lecture series (first winter semester)
Into Science Retreat (first summer semester)
Skills development
In the early stages of your doctoral studies, we recommend you focus on developing the following skills in particular:
Research methods
Presentation skills
Time and project management
Good scientific practice
The use of AI in academia
Academic writing
To top
Second and third year - Research phase
Overview
During the research phase, you will refine your argument, deepen your methods, connect with the community, and publish early results. Teaching - often in bachelor courses - can be part of this.
You will also complete curriculum-required coursework and academic activities for ECTS credits.
Steps to take
Research
Organize annual Thesis Advisory Committee (TAC) meeting
Submit your annual progress report to the SSC
Together with the annual report, you can hand in external credits
CoBeNe courses
PhD academy (every winter semester)
Skills development
You can find courses to refine your academic writing, publication strategy, and science communication on u:rise.
Also, we encourage you to pursue opportunities such as:
Public outreach
Presenting at national and international conferences
Teaching (defined by the collective agreement of UniVie employees)
Attending summer schools, workshops
Lab visits
Stay abroad
To top
Final year - Completion phase
Overview
As you progress, you will complete your research and write the doctoral thesis. Once the thesis is ready and all required coursework is complete, you submit it and await the reviews. With a positive assessment, you can register for the public defense at the respective StudiesServiceCenter. The defense consists of a presentation of your key findings followed by a discussion of the research with the examination commission. The exact procedure varies by discipline.
Steps to take
Complete research
Organize last Thesis Advisory Committee (TAC) meeting
Hand in annual progress report
Submit your written doctoral thesis
Nominate your thesis reviewer/committee
Register for your defensio
Publicly defend thesis
Conferral of PhD
CoBeNe courses
For PhD candidates nearing the final phase of their doctoral journey, we offer:
PhD Finalizing retreat
Following completion, you may want to join our alumni network.
